summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted for acute substernal chest pain radiating to the left neck and arm. Workup revealed negative troponins and no EKG changes, ruling out acute coronary syndrome. The pain was determined to be angina due to known CAD, particularly involving the LCx territory with occluded obtuse marginal arteries. Management included uptitrating amlodipine from 5 to 10 mg daily, continuing beta-blocker and antiplatelet therapy, and advising nitroglycerin use as needed. She also had acute on chronic kidney injury with admission creatinine of 2.7, likely prerenal, which improved to 2.1 with IV fluids. Transplant function was stable, with tacrolimus levels adjusted to therapeutic range. She remained asymptomatic during admission and was discharged home with follow-up planned with cardiology and nephrology.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina pectoris
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Personal history of other malignant neoplasm of skin
